To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified 100 novel human genes which are expressed in brain and other tissues and which encode proteins of various functions.

100 cDNA sequences of large human genes from brain have been determined and the predicted functions of 54 genes are related to cell signaling and communication, nucleic acid metabolism, and cell structure/motile functions.
the complete sequences of 54 cDNA clones encoding large proteins in vitro were determined, and their functional categories, expression profiles and chromosomal locations were analyzed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of novel human genes and the accumulation of information on the human gene map.
the isolation and characterization of novel cDNAs encoding large proteins.
the isolation of cDNA clones encoding large proteins, the determination of their entire coding sequences, and the analysis of their expression patterns in various human tissues and brain regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these clones encode proteins with a variety of functions, and that the expression profiles of these genes are different among tissues and brain regions.
these genes are likely to be involved in the development and maintenance of the brain, and/or the central nervous system.
the genes analyzed in this report encode novel human proteins, and the majority of these proteins are likely to be related to brain function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present cDNA clones, KIAA1775-1878, would be a valuable resource for the study of human brain functions, and that the expression profiles of the genes would be useful for the analysis of their functions.
we have obtained a large set of novel cDNA clones that encode large proteins, and the predicted gene products have been shown to be involved in the regulation of cellular processes.
the 100 cDNAs described here are useful resources for further studies of the functions of their gene products and for elucidating the mechanisms of human brain development and functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a number of novel human genes, some of which may be related to brain development and/or brain functions.
we can obtain a large number of cDNA clones that encode large proteins by size fractionation of cDNA libraries and in vitro transcription/ translation experiments.
we have identified and characterized 100 novel human genes, which are predicted to code for large proteins, and have provided a large amount of information on these genes.
